title: Video Super Resolution
summary:
Video super-resolution (VSR) is the process of generating high-resolution video frames from given low-resolution video frames. Unlike single-image super-resolution (SISR), the main goal is not only to restore more fine details while saving coarse ones, but also to preserve motion consistency. When working with video, temporal information could be used to improve upscaling quality.

Single image super-resolution methods could be used too, generating high-resolution frames independently from their neighbours, but it is less effective and introduces temporal instability. There are a few traditional methods which consider the video super-resolution task as an optimization problem. In recent years, deep learning based methods for video upscaling outperform traditional ones.

Traditional methods include frequency domain approaches where the low-resolution frame is first transformed to the frequency domain using Fourier transform to extend the spectrum of the captured signal. Other methods use wavelet transform, which helps to find similarities in neighboring local areas. Iterative back-projection methods assume some function between low-resolution and high-resolution frames and try to improve their guessed function in each step of an iterative process.

RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX VSR) is a related video scaling feature by Nvidia, released on February 28, 2023, first unveiled during CES 2023. It uses the on-board Tensor Cores to upscale browser video content in real time. Video Super Resolution is available on all Nvidia RTX-branded GPUs, supporting input resolutions from 360p to 1440p and a max output of 4K. Several deep learning architectures have been developed for VSR, including VSRnet, VESPCN, DRVSR, FRVSR, TecoGAN, and TOFlow, using techniques like optical flow estimation, motion compensation, and recurrent networks.
